changesNothing: This lane wrote exactly one file: this one. No document, artifact, checker or record in docs/coop was edited, superseded or moved. Scratch code lived outside the repository.
purpose: opensip-canonical-json-v1 is invoked at c2-plan-stage-schema.v4#planIntent.canonicalCommitment.preimage (and at PLAN-ID-V1 preimage field 13, and in every planIntentCommitment restatement) and is defined by prose fragments plus 41 pinned vectors, but by no single specification document. This file RECOVERS the function from that evidence. It does not design it: every rule below is either forced by a named vector, stated in named prose but untested by any vector, or declared UNDETERMINED. A rule with no forcing vector is never silently completed.

recoveryMethod.parseDiscipline: Every JSON document read during this recovery, and this file itself when re-walked, went through a duplicate-key-rejecting object hook (386-document corpus precedent: code-only-identity-rules.sweep.v1.json).
recoveryMethod.classificationDiscipline: Every leaf classifier tests boolean BEFORE integer. In Python, True is an instance of int; an integer-first classifier emits 1 for true, and exactly one pinned vector (valid-explicit-general-authority-forms) catches it. This is not a style preference; it is the difference between reproducing 7/7 and 6/7.
recoveryMethod.derivationDiscipline: c2-plan-stage-schema.v10 and delivery.v3/v4 are derivations and were READ RESOLVED via artifacts/check-completeness-v2.py::resolve_derivation, never as delta files. 0 resolve errors on all three.
recoveryMethod.forcingDiscipline: A baseline encoder was written from the prose alone and reproduced every pinned vector. Then, for each rule, the encoder was re-run with that single rule flipped to a plausible alternative; a vector that fails under the flip FORCES the rule. A rule no flip could make fail is recorded as prose-stated-vector-untested or undetermined, never promoted.
recoveryMethod.numericDiscipline: Adopted from plan-and-policy-identity-recipes.v1#numericRepresentationRule for this file's own bytes: no JSON number and no JSON boolean occurs at any leaf of this artifact; counts are canonical decimal strings; embedded example inputs appear as canonical text or hex, never as live JSON values.

statusVocabulary.VECTOR-FORCED: at least one named pinned vector fails under at least one named plausible alternative to the rule. The alternative and the failing count are recorded.
statusVocabulary.PROSE-STATED-VECTOR-UNTESTED: stated by named binding prose; NO pinned vector exercises it (or a rejection rule structurally admits no positive vector). An implementation that violates it still reproduces every pinned vector -- which is precisely why it is listed rather than assumed.
statusVocabulary.UNDETERMINED: more than one reading survives all prose AND all vectors. The competing readings and the vector that would settle them are recorded. Choosing one here would be invention; none is chosen.

theRecoveredFunction.name: opensip-canonical-json-v1
theRecoveredFunction.kind: deterministic JSON text canonicalisation over a closed data model, always immediately followed by a domain-separated SHA-256 in every use the corpus contains
theRecoveredFunction.dataModel: JSON objects, arrays, strings, booleans, signed integers and null ONLY. Floating-point numbers are forbidden. (Verbatim from the primary prose source.)
theRecoveredFunction.primaryProseSource: c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json#planIntent.canonicalCommitment.encoding -- the block survives all 39 operations of the v4->v9->v10->v11 derivation chain untouched and is therefore also the resolved head's text.

rules.subject: output encoding and envelope
rules.rule: The encoding of a value is the UTF-8 bytes of its canonical text. No byte-order mark, no trailing newline, no outer envelope of any kind. The digest input is exactly domainBytes || 0x00 || those bytes and nothing else.

rules.subject: whitespace
rules.rule: No insignificant whitespace anywhere: no spaces after ':' or ',', no newlines, no indentation.

rules.subject: object key ordering
rules.rule: Object members are emitted in ascending order of the member key. The comparison plane stated by prose is ascending Unicode scalar value, which is identical to ascending unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Sorting is over the unescaped key, not its serialised spelling.
rules.statusScope: FORCED against length-first ordering and against as-parsed (insertion) ordering. The PLANE is not vector-separated: every key in every pinned vector is ASCII, where Unicode-scalar-value order, UTF-8-byte order and UTF-16-code-unit order coincide. See undeterminedRegister UR-1.
rules.corroboration: CVE1 declares its map order as unsigned lexicographic order of NFC UTF-8 key bytes, the same total order, and DCM-1-core forces it there byte-exactly (reachability before references; length-first would reverse them).

rules.subject: integers
rules.rule: Integers are emitted in shortest base-10 form: no leading plus, no leading zero except the single digit 0 for zero, minus sign for negatives.
rules.statusScope: FORCED for positive integers over the exercised set {1, 4, 1000, 5000, 10000, 100000, 1048576}. The zero spelling, the negative spelling and any width bound are NOT exercised by any pinned vector: no zero and no negative integer occurs anywhere in the six families' positive vectors. See undeterminedRegister UR-2.
forcedBy: all 7 planIntentCommitment vectors (zero-padding any integer fails 7/7)

rules.subject: booleans, and boolean/integer separation
rules.rule: true and false are emitted as the lowercase literals true and false. A boolean is never an integer: classification MUST test boolean before integer, because in host languages where booleans subtype integers (Python bool is a subclass of int) an integer-first test silently emits 1 for true and the digest is wrong while every non-boolean vector still passes.
rules.statusScope: FORCED for the literal true and for the boolean-before-integer classification order, by exactly one vector. The literal false occurs ZERO times in the JSON-family vectors and is prose-stated only there; it IS byte-forced in the sibling CVE1 encoding (type byte 0x01) by snapshot-id-v1-minimal (executable false, sparseCheckout.enabled false).
forcedBy: valid-explicit-general-authority-forms (two true leaves; emitting 1 for true fails this single vector and no other)

rules.subject: null
rules.rule: null is emitted as the lowercase literal null. Explicit nulls are significant values and are never omitted.

rules.subject: empty containers
rules.rule: The empty array is the two bytes [] and the empty object is the two bytes {}, with no interior whitespace. Empty containers are PRESENT, never elided.
forcedBy: valid-explicit-general-authority-forms (between them 5 empty arrays and 19 empty objects; emitting [ ] and { } fails exactly these 3)
rules.corroboration: CVE1 side: DCM-7-empty-collection pins the empty array as 05 00000000, present not omitted.

rules.subject: string escaping
rules.rule: Strings are emitted between double quotes. Escapes are the shortest required, lowercase: \" for quote, \\ for backslash, \b \t \n \f \r for their control characters, \u00xx lowercase hex for other code points below U+0020, and NOTHING ELSE is escaped: solidus is emitted bare, and code points at U+0020 and above (including all non-ASCII) are emitted as literal UTF-8.
rules.statusScope: Only ONE clause is vector-forced: solidus-not-escaped, by valid-minimal-analysis-intent (the single '/' inside a pinned string; emitting \/ fails that one vector). Every other clause is untested: a census of every string leaf and key across all 7 JSON-family vectors finds NO double quote, NO backslash, NO control character and NO non-ASCII code point -- the only special character that occurs anywhere is '/'. The lowercase-hex clause never fires at all.
proseSources: c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json#planIntent.canonicalCommitment.encoding.strings (JSON escapes are lowercase, shortest required escapes; solidus is not escaped)
rules.whatWouldSettleIt: One pinned fixture whose strings contain a double quote, a backslash, U+0007, U+001F, a short-form control such as U+000A, an accented NFC character and a supplementary-plane character. Note the corpus DOES contain strings with embedded double quotes in the CVE1 plane (planid-v1-ci-full-providers cfg values like target_arch="aarch64"), but CVE1 is length-framed raw UTF-8 and never escapes, so those bytes force nothing about JSON escaping.

rules.subject: array order
rules.rule: Array element order is preserved exactly as given. The encoder never sorts, deduplicates or otherwise repairs an array; order-bearing versus set semantics is the owning schema's declaration, enforced at admission before encoding.

alternativesRefuted.sort every array by encoded element text: 2/7 vectors fail (valid-explicit-general-authority-forms's arrays happen to be sorted already, which is why it survives the sort flip while failing the reverse flip)

rules.corroboration: Record-framing side: PDD-ORD pins the digest an implementation produces if it accepts a mis-ordered exactCoverage list -- order is preserved, not repaired, there too.

rules.subject: Unicode normalisation
rules.rule: Prose: object keys are NFC strings; string values are NFC before encoding; keys that collide after NFC normalisation are rejected.
rules.statusScope: TWO readings survive every pinned vector: (a) NORMALISE-THEN-ENCODE: inputs are NFC-normalised by the encoder, key collisions created by normalisation are rejected; (b) REJECT-NON-NFC: a non-NFC input is rejected outright, as CVE1, the canonical-CBOR payload profile and the record-framing textComponent all explicitly do ('rejected rather than silently normalised'). Every string in every JSON-family vector is ASCII, hence already NFC, so no pinned vector separates the readings. The prose leans (a) for this encoder while every sibling encoding states (b); that divergence is real and is left standing here.
proseSources: c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json#planIntent.canonicalCommitment.totalityBoundary (rejects ... keys that collide after NFC normalisation)
resolved-inputs.v2.json#planIdContract.canonicalValueEncoding.constraints (a non-NFC string is rejected rather than silently normalised)
rules.whatWouldSettleIt: A pinned fixture whose input contains an NFD sequence (e.g. e + U+0301): a pinned commitment over it settles NORMALISE; a pinned rejection code settles REJECT. Additionally a two-key object whose keys are NFD/NFC spellings of the same string, with a pinned rejection, would force the collision clause.

rules.subject: duplicate keys
rules.rule: Duplicate object keys are rejected by the parser before any value exists to encode. No last-wins, no first-wins.
rules.statusScope: A rejection rule admits no positive golden vector (a duplicate-key input has no canonical form to pin). It is instrument-enforced corpus-wide: the section 7.5 duplicate-key parse hook, and code-only-identity-rules.sweep.v1.json measured 386 corpus documents through a duplicate-key-rejecting parse at 0 rejections. This file was likewise built and re-walked through such a hook.
proseSources: c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json#planIntent.canonicalCommitment.encoding.objects (Duplicate keys are rejected by the parser)

rules.subject: floating point
rules.rule: Floating-point numbers are outside the data model and are rejected. There is no float spelling of any committed value: 1.0 is not a spelling of 1.
rules.statusScope: Forced on the REJECTION path: three pinned mutation fixtures inject the spelling 1.0 at declared-integer positions and pin rejection (violation C2I-02, totality class float-in-declared-integer-constant). In v4 the validator's declared-integer guards run before the encoder, so the encoder-level rejection is unreachable for admitted values (totalityBoundary states this and the measured admit-then-raise finding class it closes).
rules.corroboration: Sibling encoders reject a float where an integer is declared (plan-and-policy REJ-6) because canonicalUnsignedDecimal is total only on int; CVE1 forbids floats outright; the canonical-CBOR profile forbids floating point.

rules.subject: non-string keys and non-model leaves
rules.rule: Object keys are strings; a non-string key is rejected. Any leaf outside the closed model (objects, arrays, strings, booleans, signed integers, null) is rejected.
rules.statusScope: Unreachable from JSON text input (JSON syntax admits only string keys); binding for host-side constructors. Stated by totalityBoundary; no pinned vector exists or could exist from wire input.

rules.subject: domain-separated digest and text form
rules.rule: planIntentCommitment = SHA-256( UTF8("opensip.plan-intent.v1") || 0x00 || opensip-canonical-json-v1(PlanIntent) ), rendered as sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. The NUL terminator after the domain label is structural (no admitted domain label may contain U+0000, so no two (domain, payload) pairs share a preimage).
forcedBy: all 7 planIntentCommitment vectors (omitting the NUL fails 7/7)

CD-4 (the text form is byte-consequential downstream: a sha256:-prefixed capabilityManifestId where the bare form is declared lengthens the PLAN-ID-V1 preimage from 2500 to 2507 bytes and pins a different PlanId)

jcsHazardMeasured.claim: On the pinned inputs, RFC 8785 (JCS) is byte-indistinguishable from opensip-canonical-json-v1.
jcsHazardMeasured.measurement: A faithful JCS serializer (UTF-16 code-unit key ordering, ECMAScript number serialisation, no NFC treatment, float-tolerant data model) reproduces 7/7 planIntentCommitment vectors byte-exactly, because every pinned key is ASCII, every pinned integer is a positive integer far below 2^53, and no pinned string exercises normalisation or escaping beyond the solidus clause.
jcsHazardMeasured.consequence: Green vectors do NOT certify a JCS implementation as opensip-canonical-json-v1. The two functions differ on the ordering plane (Unicode scalar value versus UTF-16 code units -- divergent for keys mixing supplementary-plane characters with U+E000..U+FFFF), on the data model (floats rejected here, serialised there), and on NFC treatment (present here in one of two undetermined forms, absent there). All three differences live entirely in the vector-untested region, which is why this file lists them as UR-1, UR-2 and CJ-R10 rather than presenting a green suite as proof.
jcsHazardMeasured.doNotDoThis: Do not implement JCS (or RFC 8949, or any named standard) and check it against the vectors. Implement the rules above. The vectors cannot see the difference today; the first non-ASCII key or first NFD string in a committed PlanIntent will.

orderingPlanes.why: The corpus canonicalises with THREE different member orders in three different encodings. They are not interchangeable, each is vector-forced in its own plane, and two of them look identical on small ASCII inputs. A recovery that unified them would reproduce zero families.

planes.encoding: opensip-canonical-json-v1 objects, and CVE1 string-keyed maps
planes.order: ascending unsigned lexicographic order of (NFC) UTF-8 key bytes == ascending Unicode scalar value of the key
planes.forcedBy: all 7 planIntentCommitment vectors (JSON side); DCM-1-core (CVE1 side: relations commit as calls, imports, reachability, references, types -- length-first would put references before reachability)

planes.order: bytewise ascending order of the DETERMINISTIC ENCODINGS of the keys (RFC 8949 core deterministic). Because the CBOR text header embeds the byte length monotonically, this is extensionally length-first-then-lexicographic for text keys.
planes.forcedBy: fact-id-v1-typescript-declares: payload commits as declared(8), container(9), declarationKind(15); raw-key lexicographic order (container first) fails the vector

planes.order: ascending bytewise order of COMPLETE ITEM RECORD BYTES, compared BEFORE the item frame is applied (evaluation-proof.v8 sortedLists rule, carried by plan-and-policy sharedPrimitives). Because field frames carry uint32be lengths, this is length-first on the leading field.
planes.forcedBy: CAP-1-core: relations commit as file(4), calls(5), types(5), clones(6)...; raw-key lexicographic fails (calls would precede file) AND framed-item comparison fails (types' 25-byte record would precede calls' 37-byte record -- measured during this recovery as a first-attempt divergence, then corrected from the published record hex)

theTwoTexts.mapOrder: Sort keys first by byte length of the deterministic-CBOR encoded text key, then lexicographically by those unsigned encoded bytes.

liveContradictionConfronted.whatTheVectorsSupport: BOTH, simultaneously, because on this data model they are the SAME total order. Measured: re-encoding both FACT-ID-V1 decodedRelationPayloads under (a) RFC 8949 bytewise-encoded-key order and (b) the mapOrder sentence produces byte-identical output, both matching the pinned canonicalRelationPayloadHex; a third order (raw key text ignoring the header) separates and FAILS vector fact-id-v1-typescript-declares.
liveContradictionConfronted.whyTheyCoincide: For definite-length, minimal-header TEXT keys, the CBOR initial byte(s) encode the byte length monotonically, so bytewise comparison of encoded keys decides by length first and content second -- which is exactly the mapOrder sentence. The two texts diverge only where a map key is not a text string (for example a byte-string key: text 'z' encodes 617a, byte h'0000' encodes 420000; RFC 8949 orders the byte string first, the length rule orders the text first). The same block forbids non-text map keys, so the divergence is UNREACHABLE inside the declared model.
liveContradictionConfronted.disposition: NOT a byte-level contradiction on the closed model; an intensional double-description with an unreachable divergence. Neither reading is selected here. If a successor ever admits non-text keys, the two sentences MUST be reconciled first, and a single vector with a byte-string key would then separate them.
liveContradictionConfronted.relatedButDistinct: The R-A/R-B sorted-list order and the CVE1 map order (see orderingPlanes) are genuinely different orders from each other; that difference is vector-forced and is not part of this contradiction.

siblingEncodings.note: These are NOT opensip-canonical-json-v1, but the 41-vector evidence set commits through them, they share the NFC/no-float/duplicate-reject discipline, and an implementer reproducing the full vector set needs all of them. Stated here exactly as the vectors force them.

encodings.string-keyed-map: 06 || u32be(entryCount) || (CVE1(key) || CVE1(value))* sorted by unsigned lexicographic order of NFC UTF-8 key bytes

CVE1.constraints: strings must already be NFC (rejected otherwise); duplicate map keys rejected; floats and byte strings forbidden (a digest travels as its lowercase-hex string form); arrays preserve order unless the owning field declares set semantics, in which case the set is sorted and deduplicated BEFORE encoding
CVE1.classificationTrap: CVE1 is TOTAL on booleans and strings: true encodes as 02 and "1" as 04 00000001 31, both well-formed. Type admission is a gate BEFORE encoding, never a property of the encoder (delivery's ADM-TYPE; NEG-TYPE-1/2 publish the wrong ids a lax admitter mints).
CVE1.forcedBy: all 24 CVE1-family reproductions in the vector index, including the 1080/2500/8208/940/924-byte pinned preimage lengths and seven decode(encode(x))==x round-trips

canonicalCborPayload.source: rust-provider-protocol.v2.json#canonicalCbor (profile) with the payload vectors pinned at fact-plane.v1.json#factRecordContractV1.vectors
canonicalCborPayload.profile: definite lengths only, minimal-length arguments, text-keyed maps, RFC 8949 core deterministic key order (see liveContradictionConfronted), no floats, no negative integers, no tags, NFC text, duplicate keys rejected, decode-reencode byte equality
canonicalCborPayload.entryIntoIdentity: the payload bytes enter FACT-ID-V1 as LOWERCASE HEX TEXT at tag 13, because CVE1 deliberately has no byte-string type

recordFramingSuite.recordShape: BARE record tag byte (0x40/0x50/0x60/0x70/0x80/0x90/0xa0/0xb0/0xc0), NO length prefix, followed by the concatenated field frames -- stated in no grammar table, recoverable only from the published hex, and confirmed here against PDD-1's completeRecordHex (the same friction implementer-litmus.v4 IL4-03 records)
recordFramingSuite.leafAndOuter: root = SHA-256(0x00 || uint64be(byteLength(record)) || record); preimage = 0x30 || C(0x31, UTF8(namespace)) || C(0x32, ASCII(domain)) || C(0x33, root); digest = SHA-256(preimage)
recordFramingSuite.textComponent: NFC-normalised UTF-8, no BOM, non-empty, at most 4096 bytes, excludes U+0000..U+001F and U+007F; non-NFC input REJECTED not normalised
recordFramingSuite.canonicalUnsignedDecimal: ASCII digits, zero is the single byte 0x30, otherwise no leading zero, no sign/separators/exponent; total only on int (a float or boolean at an integer position raises)
recordFramingSuite.sortedLists: sort complete item record bytes ascending BEFORE item framing (see orderingPlanes plane 3)
recordFramingSuite.lineageWarning: R-A (record-framed capabilityManifestId, bare-hex e109fd46... for core) is the SUPERSEDED candidate; the applied DELIVERY head commits the SAME manifest via CVE1 to 508f24c7.... Both vector sets reproduce; only DELIVERY's is the live recipe. See discrepancyRegister DR-1.

undeterminedRegister.question: Object-key ordering PLANE: Unicode scalar value (== UTF-8 bytes) or UTF-16 code units?
undeterminedRegister.state: Prose says scalar value; sibling CVE1 says UTF-8 key bytes (the same order); JCS-style UTF-16 ordering survives every pinned vector because every pinned key is ASCII. Recorded as undetermined AT THE VECTOR LEVEL while noting both prose witnesses agree on scalar-value/UTF-8.
undeterminedRegister.settlingVector: A pinned commitment over an object with keys U+E000 (private use, BMP) and U+10000 (LINEAR B SYLLABLE B008 A): scalar-value order emits U+E000 first; UTF-16 order emits U+10000 first (its surrogate pair starts D800 < E000).

undeterminedRegister.question: Integer edge forms: zero spelling, negative spelling, width bound.
undeterminedRegister.state: No pinned vector contains 0 or any negative integer; the largest exercised magnitude is 1048576. Prose gives 'no leading plus or leading zero except zero itself' and 'signed integers' with no width. CVE1 bounds ITS integers at u64/i64; whether the JSON profile shares that bound, is 2^53-bounded, or is unbounded is not determinable from any evidence in the corpus.
undeterminedRegister.settlingVector: Pinned commitments over fixtures containing 0, -1, 9223372036854775807, -9223372036854775808, and one value beyond each with a pinned accept-or-reject disposition.

undeterminedRegister.question: NFC: normalise-then-encode or reject-non-NFC (CJ-R10)?
undeterminedRegister.state: See CJ-R10. Two readings survive; siblings uniformly reject; the JSON prose reads as normalise.
undeterminedRegister.settlingVector: An NFD-string fixture with either a pinned commitment (normalise) or a pinned rejection code (reject).

undeterminedRegister.question: String escaping beyond the solidus clause (CJ-R8): short-form escapes, lowercase \u00xx, raw UTF-8 for non-ASCII.
undeterminedRegister.state: Prose-stated, zero vector coverage; a JCS-style or ASCII-only escaper is indistinguishable on today's pins except that ASCII-only escaping of non-ASCII never fires (no non-ASCII exists in the JSON family).
undeterminedRegister.settlingVector: The CJ-R08 fixture described at whatWouldSettleIt.

undeterminedRegister.question: Behaviour on lone surrogates (\ud800 unpaired in input text).
undeterminedRegister.state: Nothing in the corpus states or exercises it. The scalar-value ordering prose implies a scalar-value data model (surrogates are not scalar values), which implies rejection, but that is an implication, not a rule this file may mint.
undeterminedRegister.settlingVector: A fixture carrying an unpaired surrogate escape with a pinned rejection code.
